title: "dicer resize"
description: "Change a running instance's vCPUs and memory"
---

Changes a running instance's vCPUs or memory without restarting it, and
its definition with them, so it keeps them when it next starts.

An instance grows only as far as the `--max-vcpus` and `--max-memory` it was
started with, and its memory shrinks no further than it was started with.
vCPUs change on Cloud Hypervisor only. The guest's kernel must support
memory and CPU hotplug: virtio-mem, and `CONFIG_HOTPLUG_CPU`.

Memory is resized in steps of 2MiB. On Firecracker, resize waits for the
guest to take or give up the memory; Cloud Hypervisor cannot tell.

## Usage

```console
$ dicer resize NAME [flags]
```

## Examples

```console
$ dicer resize web --memory 4GiB
$ dicer resize web --vcpus 4 --memory 2GiB
```

## Flags

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `-m`, `--memory string` | Memory, e.g. 512MiB or 2GiB. |
| `--vcpus int32` | Number of virtual CPUs. |

## Global flags

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `-D`, `--debug` | Trace every call to the daemon on stderr (or set `$DICER_DEBUG`). |
| `-r`, `--remote string` | Daemon to talk to: a remote's name, or an address (unix:///PATH or HOST:PORT) (default `$DICER_REMOTE`, then the current remote, then local). |
| `--timeout duration` | Give up on a call to the daemon after this long, e.g. 30s (0: never; streams such as logs -f and exec are not bounded). |
